## Zoning & Development Analysis: 3400 N Central Park Ave, Chicago IL
**PIN:** 13233160400000 | **Community Area:** Irving Park (16)

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RS-3 (Residential Single-Unit – Detached House)**, per the City of Chicago's official GIS zoning layer. RS-3 is the most permissive of the three RS districts, accommodating detached houses on individual lots, differentiated primarily by minimum lot area and floor area ratio [5].

**Verify:** [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning)

---

### 2. Could You Build a Two-Flat Here?

**Possibly, under a specific exemption.** RS-3 is a single-unit detached house district — its primary purpose is detached houses [5]. A two-flat is *not* the standard permitted use. However, [1] provides a contextual exemption:

> In RS-3, the minimum lot area per dwelling unit may be reduced to **1,500 sq ft** (allowing a two-unit building) **if** 60% or more of the zoning lots fronting on the same side of the street between the two nearest intersecting streets are lawfully improved with multi-unit buildings — or if the property falls within the "Predominance of the Block" boundaries (§ 17-7-0591). This exemption allows *only* a two-unit building.

Whether the 60% threshold is met at this specific location on Central Park Ave requires a block-by-block survey and is something you'd need to verify with the **Chicago Department of Planning and Development (DPD)** or confirm with a zoning attorney.

---

### 3. Key Bulk and Density Standards (RS-3)

The context did not return the full RS-3 zone definition table (zone_definition was null), so I cannot state the precise FAR, maximum height, or all setback figures from the data. What *is* confirmed:

- **Minimum lot area per dwelling unit:** Standard RS-3 is 2,500 sq ft per unit (the baseline before the contextual two-flat exemption). Under the exemption [1], this reduces to 1,500 sq ft for a two-unit building.
- **Lot size on file:** 3,616 sq ft (assessor data). At 2,500 sq ft/unit standard, this lot supports one unit; at the 1,500 sq ft exemption, it *could* support two.
- **Other density factors:** [1] notes that off-street parking, height limits, dwelling unit sizes, and lot configuration may limit density further than the lot-area standard alone.
- **Off-street parking location:** In RS districts, parking is prohibited in side setbacks and within 20 feet of the front property line; required residential parking must be on the same zoning lot as the units served [3].

> ⚠️ **I could not confirm** the specific FAR, maximum building height, or setback dimensions for RS-3 from this data pull (zone_definition returned null). You should obtain these from the **Chicago Zoning Ordinance, Chapter 17-2-0400 and 17-2-0500**, or request a **Zoning Certificate of Use** from DPD.

### 4. Overlays and Special Designations

This parcel carries several significant overlays:

- **Special District** — The parcel is within a designated Special District. The specific district name and its practical restrictions were not returned in this data pull; you should confirm the exact district name and requirements with DPD.
- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA)** — The parcel falls within a TOD overlay area, triggered by its proximity to the **Addison Blue Line station (0.26 miles away)**. Under the Connected Communities Ordinance, this designation allows density and parking bonuses near CTA rail [transit data].
- **ADU Eligible Area** — This parcel is in an officially designated ADU-Allowed RS Area under [2] (§ 17-7-0570–17-7-0574), which is highly significant for question 6 below.
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone** — Any development triggering ARO thresholds in this zone may require affordable unit set-asides or in-lieu fees. Irving Park has 2 ARO projects totaling 65 affordable units in the community area (Independence Apts. at 4022 N. Elston, 14 senior units; Senior Residence at Kedzie at 4054 N. Kedzie, 51 senior units).
- **No Planned Development** — Not in a Planned Development.
- **No Landmark/Historic District** — Not a Chicago Landmark building, not in a landmark district, not in a historic district, and not on the National Register of Historic Places.
- **No Special Service Area (SSA)** — No SSA applies.
- **Flood Zone X** — Designated FEMA Zone X ("Area of Minimal Flood Hazard") — not a Special Flood Hazard Area; flood insurance is not typically required.
- **Brownfield Note:** Two nearby brownfield sites are registered — BNSF Little Village Paseo Segment 1 (EPA ID: 110071982538) and Segment 2 (EPA ID: 110071982539) — located in the vicinity. Environmental due diligence (Phase I ESA) may be advisable depending on your project scope.

---

### 5. Parking Requirements and Transit-Related Reductions

Under [3], RS district parking rules require:

- Required off-street parking must be on the **same zoning lot** as the dwelling units served.
- Parking is **prohibited in side setbacks** and within a **20-foot front setback** (but is permitted in a required side setback when accessed by a permitted driveway from the front property line).
- Required non-residential parking (e.g., religious assembly) may be located off-site up to 600 feet away only via **special use approval** [3].

**TOD Parking Reduction:** Because this parcel is within a **CTA TOD overlay** (Addison Blue Line, 0.26 mi), the Connected Communities Ordinance may allow reduced or waived parking minimums for residential development. The exact reduction depends on the use and project type — confirm the specific reduction with DPD or review Chicago Municipal Code § 17-10-0102.

**Coach house parking:** Per [4], accessory parking required for the principal residential building may be reduced or waived for coach houses via administrative adjustment (§ 17-13-1003-OO), and coach houses themselves may be established without accessory parking to serve the coach house unit.

---

### 6. Coach House / Additional Dwelling Unit (ADU)

**Yes — this is a strong candidate for an ADU**, and this is one of the most notable findings for this parcel.

**This parcel is in an officially designated ADU-Allowed RS Area** [2], which means both **conversion units** (basement/attic ADUs) and **coach houses** (detached accessory dwelling units) may be eligible. Key conditions and limits under [4] and [2]:

- A building permit for a new coach house in an RS district **may only be issued if the lot complies with § 17-7-0570** [4] — i.e., it must be in an ADU-Allowed RS Area, which this parcel is.
- Coach houses **may not exceed 22 feet in building height** [4].
- Rooftop features also may not exceed 22 feet above grade [4].
- At least **3 feet of unobstructed open space** must be provided between the coach house and at least one side property line for the entire length of the building wall (exception: when a side property line abuts an alley or street) [4].
- A coach house in B or C districts must be in the rear 30 feet of lot depth — but this parcel is RS, so that restriction does not apply [4].
- Coach houses may be built **without accessory parking** to serve the coach house unit itself [4].
- The ADU program is **enforced by the Department of Housing** at the time of ADU pre-certification (§ 2-44-106(g)) [2].
- Individual ADU-Allowed RS Areas may impose additional limitations on conversion units and coach houses beyond the baseline [2] — you must verify whether any area-specific restrictions apply to this particular zone segment.
